text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliament to examine three new projects to ammend parts of customs law.
- Suzanne Mubarak tells al-Ahram of national project to build 100 health units to care for mothers.
- Egypt to promote its successful industrial products abroad.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa discusses peace process with delegation from U.S. congress.
- Egypt's ambassador in London says privatisation is the basis of economic reform.
- Netanyahu's aide Dore Gold due in Cairo today to discuss problem of Hebron pullout and developments in Palestinian-Israeli peace talks.
- Mubarak's adviser Osama el-Baz in Washington to examine ways to boost peace negotiations.

- Profits to be distributed among 1.2 million workers next week. Special bonuses for exceptional workers. Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says will sack board of directors of any company that incurs losses in two consecutive years.
- Moussa says Jewish settlements are big mistake aimed at handicapping peace process.
- Cabinet to discuss projects and laws aimed at encouraging investment.
- Israeli radio reports U.S.-Egyptian plan to solve Hebron problem.
- Five ministers in meeting with investors announce ways to remove obstacles hindering investment. A thousand factories to be built that will create 80,000 jobs.
- Man commits suicide because he could not keep up with demands of his fiancee and her family.
- More provocative statements from Israeli prime minister. New settlement to be built in East Jerusalem. Netanyahu promises to prevent creation of Palestinian state.
